description: Do installs stick around? Cohort retention, lifecycle and tenure for the Dozzle beacon.

options.content:
**An install = one Dozzle `ServerID`.** Beacons that report no `ServerID` are excluded —
they all share the empty key and would otherwise roll up into a single phantom install
(~6% of events). Everything here reads the `daily_client_*` continuous aggregates, so it
survives the 1-year retention policy on the raw `beacon` table. Weeks start Monday, and
the most recent week is partial.

panels.title: Weekly active installs
panels.description: Distinct installs sending an events beacon in the last 7 days.

panels.title: Monthly active installs
panels.description: Distinct installs sending an events beacon in the last 28 days.

panels.title: Stickiness (WAU / MAU)
panels.description: Share of the monthly base that shows up in a given week. Higher means installs are used habitually rather than occasionally.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(100.0 * count(DISTINCT client_id) FILTER (WHERE day > now() - interval '7 days')
                   / NULLIF(count(DISTINCT client_id), 0), 1) AS "WAU / MAU"
FROM daily_client_events
WHERE client_id <> '' AND day > now() - interval '28 days';

panels.title: New installs (28d)
panels.description: Installs whose very first beacon of any kind landed in the last 28 days.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
  activation AS (
    SELECT client_id, min(day) AS activated
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY client_id
  )
SELECT count(*) AS "New installs (28d)"
FROM activation
WHERE activated > now() - interval '28 days';

panels.title: Weekly cohort retention
panels.description: Each row is the set of installs that first reported in that week. WN is the share of them still sending beacons N weeks later. Read down a column to see whether newer cohorts retain better than older ones.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
  activation AS (
    SELECT client_id, min(day) AS activated
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY client_id
  ),
  cohorts AS (
    -- Filter on the cohort *week*, not the activation timestamp: a range starting
    -- mid-week would otherwise drop installs from cohort_size while still counting them
    -- as active below, which pushes retention over 100%.
    SELECT cohort_week, count(*) AS cohort_size
    FROM (SELECT date_trunc('week', activated) AS cohort_week FROM activation) a
    WHERE $__timeFilter(cohort_week)
    GROUP BY 1
  ),
  activity AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
           date_trunc('week', a.activated) AS cohort_week,
           e.client_id,
           ((date_trunc('week', e.day)::date - date_trunc('week', a.activated)::date) / 7)::int AS week_index
    FROM daily_client_events e
    JOIN activation a ON a.client_id = e.client_id
    WHERE e.client_id <> ''
      AND date_trunc('week', a.activated) IN (SELECT cohort_week FROM cohorts)
  ),
  counts AS (
    SELECT cohort_week, week_index, count(*) AS installs
    FROM activity
    WHERE week_index BETWEEN 0 AND 12
    GROUP BY 1, 2
  )
SELECT to_char(c.cohort_week, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "Cohort (week of)",
       c.cohort_size AS "Installs",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 1) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W1",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 2) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W2",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 3) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W3",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 4) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W4",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 5) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W5",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 6) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W6",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 7) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W7",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 8) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W8",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 9) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W9",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 10) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W10",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 11) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W11",
       round(100.0 * max(k.installs) FILTER (WHERE k.week_index = 12) / c.cohort_size, 1) AS "W12"
FROM cohorts c
LEFT JOIN counts k ON k.cohort_week = c.cohort_week
GROUP BY c.cohort_week, c.cohort_size
ORDER BY c.cohort_week DESC;

panels.title: Average retention curve
panels.description: The cohort table collapsed into one line: the share of a cohort still active N weeks after install, averaged over every cohort in range that has actually lived that long. This is the shape to move.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
  activation AS (
    SELECT client_id, min(day) AS activated
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY client_id
  ),
  cohorts AS (
    -- Filter on the cohort *week*, not the activation timestamp: a range starting
    -- mid-week would otherwise drop installs from cohort_size while still counting them
    -- as active below, which pushes retention over 100%.
    SELECT cohort_week, count(*) AS cohort_size
    FROM (SELECT date_trunc('week', activated) AS cohort_week FROM activation) a
    WHERE $__timeFilter(cohort_week)
    GROUP BY 1
  ),
  activity AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
           date_trunc('week', a.activated) AS cohort_week,
           e.client_id,
           ((date_trunc('week', e.day)::date - date_trunc('week', a.activated)::date) / 7)::int AS week_index
    FROM daily_client_events e
    JOIN activation a ON a.client_id = e.client_id
    WHERE e.client_id <> ''
      AND date_trunc('week', a.activated) IN (SELECT cohort_week FROM cohorts)
  ),
  counts AS (
    SELECT cohort_week, week_index, count(*) AS installs
    FROM activity
    WHERE week_index BETWEEN 0 AND 12
    GROUP BY 1, 2
  )
SELECT 'W' || k.week_index AS "Weeks since install",
       round(avg(100.0 * k.installs / c.cohort_size), 1) AS "Installs still active"
FROM counts k
JOIN cohorts c ON c.cohort_week = k.cohort_week
-- Only count a cohort at week N once it has actually lived N weeks, otherwise young
-- cohorts drag the tail of the curve towards zero.
WHERE c.cohort_week <= now() - ((k.week_index + 1) || ' weeks')::interval
GROUP BY k.week_index
ORDER BY k.week_index;

panels.title: Week 1 / 4 / 12 retention by cohort
panels.description: Same numbers as three columns of the table, plotted over time. Diverging lines mean a release changed how well new installs stick.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
  activation AS (
    SELECT client_id, min(day) AS activated
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY client_id
  ),
  cohorts AS (
    -- Filter on the cohort *week*, not the activation timestamp: a range starting
    -- mid-week would otherwise drop installs from cohort_size while still counting them
    -- as active below, which pushes retention over 100%.
    SELECT cohort_week, count(*) AS cohort_size
    FROM (SELECT date_trunc('week', activated) AS cohort_week FROM activation) a
    WHERE $__timeFilter(cohort_week)
    GROUP BY 1
  ),
  activity AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
           date_trunc('week', a.activated) AS cohort_week,
           e.client_id,
           ((date_trunc('week', e.day)::date - date_trunc('week', a.activated)::date) / 7)::int AS week_index
    FROM daily_client_events e
    JOIN activation a ON a.client_id = e.client_id
    WHERE e.client_id <> ''
      AND date_trunc('week', a.activated) IN (SELECT cohort_week FROM cohorts)
  ),
  counts AS (
    SELECT cohort_week, week_index, count(*) AS installs
    FROM activity
    WHERE week_index BETWEEN 0 AND 12
    GROUP BY 1, 2
  )
SELECT k.cohort_week AS time,
       'Week ' || k.week_index AS metric,
       round(100.0 * k.installs / c.cohort_size, 1) AS value
FROM counts k
JOIN cohorts c ON c.cohort_week = k.cohort_week
WHERE k.week_index IN (1, 4, 12)
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Install lifecycle
panels.description: New = first ever seen. Retained = also active last week. Resurrected = active before, but not last week. Churned (below the axis) = active last week, silent this week. The net of the four bars is week-over-week growth.

targets.rawSql:
WITH weekly AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('week', day) AS week, client_id
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
      AND day >  $__timeFrom()::timestamptz - interval '8 days'
      AND day <= $__timeTo()::timestamptz
  ),
  first_seen AS (
    SELECT client_id, date_trunc('week', min(day)) AS first_week
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY 1
  ),
  f AS (
    SELECT w.week, w.client_id, fs.first_week,
           lag(w.week) OVER (PARTITION BY w.client_id ORDER BY w.week) AS prev_week
    FROM weekly w
    JOIN first_seen fs ON fs.client_id = w.client_id
  )
SELECT week AS time,
       CASE WHEN week = first_week                      THEN 'New'
            WHEN prev_week = week - interval '7 days'   THEN 'Retained'
            ELSE 'Resurrected' END AS metric,
       count(*)::bigint AS value
FROM f
WHERE $__timeFilter(week)
GROUP BY 1, 2
UNION ALL
SELECT f.week + interval '7 days' AS time,
       'Churned' AS metric,
       -count(*)::bigint AS value
FROM f
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM weekly n
                  WHERE n.client_id = f.client_id
                    AND n.week = f.week + interval '7 days')
  AND f.week + interval '7 days' < date_trunc('week', $__timeTo()::timestamptz)
  AND $__timeFilter(f.week + interval '7 days')
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Active installs by tenure
panels.description: The active base split by how long ago each install first reported. A base that is mostly under a month old is churning through users; a thickening 1-year+ band is real retention.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
  activation AS (
    SELECT client_id, min(day) AS activated
    FROM daily_client_events
    WHERE client_id <> ''
    GROUP BY client_id
  ),
  weekly AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT date_trunc('week', e.day) AS week, e.client_id, a.activated
    FROM daily_client_events e
    JOIN activation a ON a.client_id = e.client_id
    WHERE e.client_id <> '' AND $__timeFilter(e.day)
  )
SELECT week AS time,
       CASE WHEN week - activated < interval '7 days'   THEN '1 - under a week'
            WHEN week - activated < interval '28 days'  THEN '2 - 1 to 4 weeks'
            WHEN week - activated < interval '90 days'  THEN '3 - 1 to 3 months'
            WHEN week - activated < interval '365 days' THEN '4 - 3 to 12 months'
            ELSE '5 - over a year' END AS metric,
       count(*)::bigint AS value
FROM weekly
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1;
